title: How do we write four fractions in lowest terms?
description: Seventeen over fifty one, sixty four over one hundred forty four, one hundred twenty six over one hundred forty seven and five hundred twenty five over one hundred twelve are each divided by a number that goes into both. Each result is checked to share no factor except one.
teaching_notes: One idea: find the number that goes into both the top and the bottom and divide both by it. Watch for students who stop after one small division while a factor is still shared.

source: Figure it Out Q1 (section 7.6, fourth block)
video_script.why: A learner reduces four fractions to lowest terms by dividing the top and the bottom by the same number.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own four fractions
video_script.anchor: four fractions written in a row on the board: 17/51, 64/144, 126/147 and 525/112
video_script.payoff_line: In lowest terms the fractions are one third, four ninths, six sevenths and seventy five over sixteen

final_answer.spoken: one third, four ninths, six sevenths and seventy five over sixteen

video_script.fraction_reading: seventeen over fifty one, sixty four over one hundred forty four, one hundred twenty six over one hundred forty seven, five hundred twenty five over one hundred twelve
maths_rules: check: 1 and 3, 4 and 9, 6 and 7, 75 and 16 share no factor except 1; 75 = 3 × 5 × 5 and 16 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2
video_script.design: One idea: split the top and the bottom into the shared number times something, then divide by the shared number. The four fractions stay in a row and each is reduced in turn.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about reducing four fractions.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you write each one in its smallest form?

beats.on_screen: the four fractions stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: an arrow marked divide by the same number joins a fraction to a smaller fraction; a long strip and a short strip stay the same length

narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>To reduce a fraction, divide its top and its bottom by the same number.
<bookmark mark='bigger'/>The bigger that number is, the sooner we reach the smallest form.

marks.given: the four given fractions are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four fractions, each with a top and a bottom number.

beats.on_screen: To find: each fraction in lowest terms

marks.find: the question to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each fraction in lowest terms.

marks.split: 51 is split into 3 × 17 and an arrow marked ÷ 17 joins 17/51 to 1/3

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, the first fraction is seventeen over fifty one.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Fifty one is three times seventeen, so divide both by seventeen. We get one third.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Step two, the next is sixty four over one hundred forty four.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Sixty four is four times sixteen, and one hundred forty four is nine times sixteen.
<bookmark mark='divide'/>Dividing both by sixteen gives four ninths.

marks.bottom: 147 is split into 7 × 21 and an arrow marked ÷ 21 joins 126/147 to 6/7

narration: <bookmark mark='third'/>Step three, the third fraction is one hundred twenty six over one hundred forty seven.
<bookmark mark='top'/>One hundred twenty six is six times twenty one.
<bookmark mark='bottom'/>One hundred forty seven is seven times twenty one, so we get six sevenths.

marks.bottom: 112 is split into 16 × 7 and an arrow marked ÷ 7 joins 525/112 to 75/16

narration: <bookmark mark='last'/>Step four, the last fraction is five hundred twenty five over one hundred twelve.
<bookmark mark='top'/>Five hundred twenty five is seventy five times seven.
<bookmark mark='bottom'/>One hundred twelve is sixteen times seven. Dividing by seven gives seventy five over sixteen.

beats.on_screen: Check: 75 = 3 × 5 × 5 and 16 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 share nothing; the other three pairs share only 1

marks.check: the factors of 75 and 16 are listed side by side and nothing is shared
marks.others: the other three pairs are ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, look at each new top and bottom. Seventy five has the factors three and five, and sixteen has only two.
<bookmark mark='others'/>The other three pairs also share no factor except one.

marks.pay: the four answers are written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>In lowest terms the fractions are one third, four ninths, six sevenths and seventy five over sixteen.
